categories.name: It works
categories.notes: Build OK with 0 errors and 10 warnings, all the scaffold's ImageSharp advisories, so none added by the model. / returns 200 through the '/' domain on Blog and lists both posts as cards with a cropped listing image, date, excerpt and a 'Read more' link. Both posts render every block (rich text, image, quote) with no errors. All 4 media items are the provided Unsplash photos, imported into a 'Blog Images' folder and served via signed GetCropUrl URLs (6/6 load). All content is published.

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: richTextBlock, imageBlock and quoteBlock are element types in Blocks. blogFrontPage and blogPost are document types in Pages, and siteRoot is in Repositories. The 'Blog Block Grid' data type is in Custom/ and is used for body on both pages. siteRoot is the only type allowed at root, the allowed children are siteRoot→blogFrontPage→blogPost, and templates are assigned. publishDate, excerpt and listingImage are real properties. There are no compositions and no duplicate or orphaned types.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: Both templates use Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync, and the scaffold's blockgrid partials are untouched. Each block has one adapter that maps BlockGridItem<T> to a plain model in Models/Blocks and calls Component.InvokeAsync. The RichText/Image/Quote ViewComponents render Umbraco-free Default.cshtml views. GetCropUrl is used, and Program.cs and appsettings are untouched. -1: the richTextBlock adapter first used the typed Model.Content.Text, then swapped it for an untyped Value("text") with a Newtonsoft JObject / IHtmlEncodedString / ToString() fallback chain. That bypasses the ModelsBuilder property. Minor: both templates duplicate the full HTML shell (Layout = null).

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Content 2/6: both posts are on topic but very thin, about 75-85 words each across 2-3 short paragraphs. The quotes are invented and attributed to 'Claude Code Team' and 'Umbraco Team'. Each post uses 4 blocks and relevant photos. Presentation 3/4: clean Tailwind layout with title, card listing, back link, footer and captioned images. However, `prose` does nothing without the typography plugin, so rich-text paragraphs run together with no spacing.

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: Channel 3/3: 42 MCP calls (35 writes), with no Management API, database, migration or browser use, and the recipe's order was followed (no warnings). The process.stayedInFolder FAIL is a false positive: every listed path is a project file under the /x/ drive prefix, and the only other reads are the harness's own background-task outputs. Report 1.5/2: accurate overall and verified with curl, but it says post 1 is 'rich text, image, rich text, quote', while the real order is rich text, rich text, quote, image (one image add failed and was re-added at the end). The report is also printed twice.

summary: Devstral 2 followed the MCP recipe cleanly and built a fully working, correctly modeled block-grid blog: 3 blocks, the adapter → plain model → ViewComponent pipeline, a '/' domain and imported Unsplash media. 42/43 checks pass; the one FAIL is a false positive. The weak spots are very thin posts (~80 words each, invented quotes), a hacky untyped rich-text adapter, and rich text without paragraph spacing.
strengths: Build is clean apart from the scaffold's own warnings, all pages return 200, and every block renders
Textbook adapter → plain model → ViewComponent pipeline with GetCropUrl and Umbraco-free component views
Schema modeled correctly: folders, element vs document, Custom/ block grid data type, allowed children, templates, real metadata properties
MCP-only process that followed the recipe's order and verified the output with curl

issues.text: Posts are very thin: about 75-85 words each in 2-3 short paragraphs, with invented quotes attributed to 'Claude Code Team' / 'Umbraco Team' (/why-mcp-servers-are-awesome/, /mcp-and-umbraco-integration/)

The richTextBlock adapter reads Value("text") untyped and parses it as a Newtonsoft JObject, with fallbacks, instead of using the typed Model.Content.Text (Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/richTextBlock.cshtml)
`prose` has no effect without @tailwindcss/typography, so rich-text paragraphs have no spacing between them (Views/blogPost.cshtml, Views/Shared/Components/RichText/Default.cshtml)
Final report misstates post 1's block order and is printed twice
Both templates duplicate the full HTML shell with Layout = null instead of sharing a layout (Views/blogFrontPage.cshtml, Views/blogPost.cshtml)
